title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 12)
summary: NH closes Book One of Hagakure, covering unwavering self-confidence, keeping the big picture, punishment as compassion, enduring hardship as the essence of the warrior, devotion despite mediocre talent, and things only understood with maturity or effort. He ties these to enjoying training and projecting it over years.
claims: Train with all your might and believe your valour is beyond compare; the world will undervalue you enough without your help
Self-confidence creates momentum: think of yourself as a sun in the darkness, and express that belief in your training
Keep the big picture; small details matter mainly because they can become a thorn in your psyche
Real correction is compassionate; telling someone they're fine when they're not misguides them
Pure positive reinforcement has limits; some kids need negativity, and NH was one who needed the world to kick him
Doing everything for monetary gain enslaves you; people with too many possessions become possessed by them
Enduring hardship is what makes a warrior; each challenge overcome makes smaller ones feel like nothing
People who avoid pain at all costs become more vulnerable and attract hardship, since predators target the weak
Someone will always be better, sometimes without working for it; complaining is a loser's mindset, focus only on what you do
Enjoy training; you get more results when you stop obsessing over results because you can focus on the process
People obsessed with one rep or one weight program poorly; training must be projected years ahead, not six weeks
The value of hard work is among the most important things to learn; once you see years of effort pay off you know you can achieve anything
Refusing to accept that something exists because you can't explain it is immature
